class S2D4P.data.dataloader.Dataloader(config: DataloaderConfigABC, dataset: Dataset, collate_fn: Callable, rank: int = 0, world_size: int = 1, shuffle: bool | None = None, return_spatial_mask: bool = False)

Bases: object

Wrapper around a PyTorch data loader with distributed sampling support.

Constructs a PyTorch DataLoader from the dataset and loader configuration, using a distributed sampler when multiple processes participate.

Parameters:

  • config (DataloaderConfigABC) – Configuration defining batching, workers, memory, and sampling behavior.

  • dataset (Dataset) – Dataset providing individual samples.

  • collate_fn (Callable) – Function used to combine individual samples into batches.

  • rank (int) – Rank of the current distributed process.

  • world_size (int) – Number of distributed processes participating in data loading.

  • shuffle (bool | None) – Whether samples are shuffled. If None, an appropriate default is selected from the distributed configuration.

  • return_spatial_mask (bool) – Whether the collation function constructs spatial validity masks.

final select_requested_times(requested_slice: slice) → DataArray

Select available initialization times within a requested year range.

Available times are sorted before selection. Requested start and stop years are validated against the temporal coverage of the dataset.

Parameters:

requested_slice (slice) – Inclusive year range used to select initialization times. Slice bounds may be integers, integer strings, or None.

Returns:

Available initialization times falling within the requested year range.

Return type:

xr.DataArray

Raises:

  • ValueError – If the requested range extends beyond available years, contains no available times, or contains an invalid year string.

  • TypeError – If a year bound is neither an integer, string, nor None.

S2D4P.data.utils module

S2D4P.data.utils.add_lead_times(init_times: ndarray | DataArray, lead_times: ndarray | DataArray, lead_time_resolution: Literal['day', 'month'] = 'month') → ndarray

Calculate target times from paired initialization and lead times.

Lead times are one-based, so a lead time of one corresponds to the initialization time itself. NumPy datetime and CFTime calendars are supported.

Parameters:

  • init_times (np.ndarray | xr.DataArray) – One-dimensional initialization times.

  • lead_times (np.ndarray | xr.DataArray) – One-dimensional integer-valued lead times paired element-wise with init_times.

  • lead_time_resolution (lead_time_unit) – Temporal unit used to interpret lead-time offsets.

Returns:

Target times corresponding element-wise to initialization and lead times.

Return type:

np.ndarray

Raises:

  • TypeError – If initialization times are neither NumPy datetime nor CFTime values.

  • ValueError – If inputs are not one-dimensional, have different shapes, lead times are not integer-valued or positive, or the lead-time resolution is unsupported.

S2D4P.data.utils.assign_datetime_init_time(ds: Dataset | DataArray, init_time_dim: str = 'time', calendar: str | None = None) → Dataset | DataArray

Replace integer initialization years with datetime coordinates.

Integer year coordinates are converted to January 1 timestamps. Standard NumPy datetime values are used by default, while specifying a calendar produces CFTime coordinates.

Parameters:

  • ds (xr.Dataset | xr.DataArray) – Data containing an integer initialization-year coordinate.

  • init_time_dim (str) – Name of the initialization-time coordinate.

  • calendar (str | None) – CFTime calendar used to construct timestamps. If None, NumPy datetime64 values are created.

Returns:

Data with initialization years replaced by datetime coordinates.

Return type:

xr.Dataset | xr.DataArray

Raises:

  • TypeError – If the initialization-time coordinate does not contain integer years.

  • ValueError – If the initialization-time coordinate is absent.

S2D4P.data.utils.infer_time_resolution(times: DatetimeIndex | CFTimeIndex) → Literal['day', 'month', 'year']

Infer temporal resolution from consecutive timestamps.

The minimum spacing between consecutive times determines the reported resolution. Spacings below 28 days are considered daily, spacings below 365 days are considered monthly, and larger spacings are considered yearly.

Parameters:

times (pd.DatetimeIndex | xr.CFTimeIndex) – Ordered timestamps from which temporal resolution is inferred.

Returns:

Inferred "day", "month", or "year" resolution.

Return type:

TimeFrequency

Raises:

ValueError – If fewer than two timestamps are provided.

S2D4P.data.utils.suppress_stderr() → Iterator[None]

Temporarily suppress process-level standard error output.

The standard-error file descriptor is redirected to the operating system null device for the duration of the context and restored afterward.

Yields:

None – Control to the code executed while standard error is suppressed.

S2D4P.data.weights module

class S2D4P.data.weights.WeightsConfig(spatial_method: Literal['uniform', 'cosine_lat'] = 'uniform', variable_weights: dict[str, float] | None = None, load_dir: Path | str | None = None)

Bases: object

Configuration for spatial and variable loss weights.

Weights can be generated from target coordinates or loaded from an existing NetCDF file. Spatial weighting can be uniform or scaled by the cosine of latitude, and optional variable-specific weights can be applied along the channel dimension.

Parameters:

  • spatial_method (Spatialmethod) – Spatial weighting method. Supported values are "uniform" and "cosine_lat".

  • variable_weights (dict[str, float] | None) – Mapping from target variable names to multiplicative weights. If provided, entries must match the target channels exactly.

  • load_dir (Path | str | None) – Path to a previously saved weights file. If None, weights are generated from the target coordinates.

build_weights(target_coords: dict, Flattennanremover: Flattennanremove | None = None, save=True, save_path: Path | str | None = None, save_name: str | None = None)

Build or load weights for target variables and spatial coordinates.

When load_dir is configured, stored weights are loaded and validated against the target coordinates. Otherwise, weights are initialized uniformly and optional cosine-latitude and variable-specific weighting are applied. Generated weights can be saved to disk and optionally transformed to a fitted flattened representation.

Parameters:

  • target_coords (dict) – Mapping from target dimension names to their coordinate values.

  • Flattennanremover (Flattennanremove | None) – Optional fitted flattening preprocessor applied to the final weights.

  • save (bool) – Whether newly generated weights are saved to disk.

  • save_path (Path | str | None) – Directory in which generated weights are saved. If None, the current experiment directory is used.

  • save_name (str | None) – Filename used when saving generated weights. If None, "spatial_weights.nc" is used.

Returns:

Weight array aligned with the target coordinates and optionally transformed to the flattened target representation.

Return type:

xr.DataArray

Raises:

ValueError – If loaded weights do not match the target coordinates, cosine-latitude weighting is requested without a latitude coordinate, variable weights do not exactly match the target channels, or the resulting weights contain negative, missing, or infinite values.

load_dir: Path | str | None = None
spatial_method: Literal['uniform', 'cosine_lat'] = 'uniform'
variable_weights: dict[str, float] | None = None
